[#](url) submission name:
roro_perframe_hnerv

# upload zipped `archive.zip`
<!-- drag and drop archive.zip into this description so curl -L works -->
ATTACH archive.zip HERE

# report.txt
```
=== Evaluation results over 600 samples ===
  Average PoseNet Distortion: 0.00140617
  Average SegNet Distortion: 0.00252939
  Submission file size: 164,744 bytes
  Original uncompressed size: 37,545,489 bytes
  Compression Rate: 0.00438785
  Final score: 100*segnet_dist + sqrt(10*posenet_dist) + 25*rate = 0.48
```

# does your submission require gpu for evaluation (inflation)?
no

# did you include the compression script? and want it to be merged?
yes

# is this submission competitive or innovative? explain why
Innovative. It uses a per frame neural representation rather than the per pair latent plus two head decoder that the current leaderboard entries use. Every frame gets its own latent vector decoded independently by a shared dense NeRV style decoder, which keeps true frame to frame motion and helps the PoseNet term. The most useful finding was that the challenge rgb to yuv preprocessing is wrapped in a no gradient context and written in place, which silently severs the PoseNet gradient during training. A value identical differentiable replacement, patched in only during training, unlocked pose learning and was the single biggest improvement. The result is 0.48, which does not beat the top entry, but the architecture and the analysis are new to the board.

# additional comments
The full writeup is in submissions/roro_perframe_hnerv/README.md. The training pipeline (per frame latents, a smooth disagreement SegNet loss, a concave PoseNet loss, weight EMA, a Muon optimizer on the conv weights, and INT6 quantization aware training) is in src/train.py, and compress.sh reproduces the archive from scratch.
[archive.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29439882/archive.zip)
